In a dramatic turn of events, law enforcement officials discovered 14 improvised explosive devices while serving a search warrant in Old Fort, Tennessee, on Friday.

The operation targeted a 54-year-old man who allegedly threatened to kill public officials and attempted to detonate the explosive devices during his arrest, according to the Polk County Sheriff’s Office.
The incident unfolded as detectives and deputies descended on the suspect’s residence, located approximately 45 miles east of Chattanooga.
Upon apprehending the individual, officers detected “something smoldering” in the bedroom where he had taken refuge.
Recognizing the potential danger, they immediately evacuated the home.
Following the evacuation, bomb squad officers, alongside agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), conducted a thorough search of the premises.
Their efforts unveiled a total of 14 improvised explosive devices, raising serious safety concerns for the surrounding community.
The suspect now faces multiple charges, including 11 counts of attempted first-degree murder, 14 counts of prohibited weapons, and one count of possession of explosive components.
He is being held at the Polk County Jail, though authorities were unable to confirm if he has legal representation at this time.
Additionally, it has been reported that the suspect had active warrants out against him for making threats against public officials and law enforcement officers within the county.
Despite the dangerous nature of the situation, Chattanooga police spokesperson Elisa Myzal confirmed that none of the explosive devices detonated during the incident.
However, she refrained from providing details regarding the suspect’s specific threats to officials or whether his arrest was prompted by an imminent danger assessment by agents.
As the investigation continues, inquiries about the incident have been directed to the sheriff’s office, although officials indicated that no one was available for comment at this time.
